source_text: Ὅτι οὐ δεῖ διάκονον ἔμπροσθεν πρεσβυτέρου καθέζεσθαι, ἀλλὰ μετὰ κελεύσεως τοῦ πρεσβυτέρου καθέζεσθαι. Ὁμοίως δὲ ἔχειν τιμὴν καὶ τοὺς διακόνους ὑπὸ τῶν ὑπηρετῶν καὶ πάντων τῶν κληρικῶν.
orientation: The council is issuing a rule about the seating order and honor of deacons relative to presbyters and other clergy.
pass_a_gloss: That not [it] is necessary [for] a deacon before [an] elder to sit down, but with [the] command [of] the elder to sit down. Likewise [it] is necessary [for them] to have honor also the deacons from the servants and all the clerics.

choices.english: with the permission of the presbyter
choices.why: κέλευσις here means authorization or leave, not a direct command; 'permission' captures the deacon's subordinate seating.
rejected: at the command of the presbyter

choices.why: The infinitive with δεῖ understood carries a prescriptive force; 'should have honor' keeps the deontic sense.
The brief identifies ὑπηρέται as attendants ranked below deacons; 'servants' matches the cast list.
The phrase includes every clerical rank; 'all the clergy' is the plain collective rendering.

pass_b_english: A deacon must not sit in front of a presbyter, but may sit only with the presbyter's permission. Likewise, the deacons should receive honor from the servants and from all the clergy.

last_rejected.quote: Likewise, the deacons should receive honor from the servants and from all the clergy.
last_rejected.source_quote: Ὁμοίως δὲ ἔχειν τιμὴν καὶ τοὺς διακόνους ὑπὸ τῶν ὑπηρετῶν καὶ πάντων τῶν κληρικῶν
last_rejected.why: Source says deacons are to receive honor FROM servants and all clergy; 'ὑπό' marks servants/clergy as those giving honor, not receiving it.
last_rejected.fix: Likewise, the deacons are to receive honor from the servants and from all the clergy.
last_rejected.ruling: English 'from' correctly renders ὑπό + genitive as agent: honor received FROM servants/clergy. No error.
